The solid arc belongs to the ellipse

$$
x=4\cos\theta,\qquad y=3\sin\theta.
$$

Find the **closed interval** of $\theta$ that traces exactly the solid arc once. Use endpoints between $0$ and $2\pi$, including both endpoints of the arc.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The ellipse has center $(0,0)$, horizontal radius $4$ and vertical radius $3$. The standard parametrization travels counterclockwise from the rightmost point. Substituting the cardinal parameter values gives

$$
\begin{array}{c|c}\theta &(x,y)\\\hline 0 & (4,0) \\ \frac{\pi}{2} & (0,3) \\ \pi & (-4,0) \\ \frac{3\pi}{2} & (0,-3) \\ 2\pi & (4,0)\end{array}
$$

The **solid arc** is the upper part relative to the center. It starts at $(4,0)$ when $\theta=0$ and ends at $(-4,0)$ when $\theta=\pi$. The counterclockwise traversal between these endpoints follows exactly the solid part, including both endpoints.

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-z7ii9jxi/17592186152190/50fcc4b4b6c933e5b9f0823e-solution.png)

Here $\theta$ is the angle on the scaled unit circle $((x-h)/a,(y-k)/b)$; it is generally different from the geometric angle on the ellipse. The required restricted parametrization is

$$
x=4\cos\theta,\qquad y=3\sin\theta,\qquad \theta \in [0,\pi].
$$
